### Wagner-Meerwein Rearrangement

**Definition:**
The Wagner-Meerwein rearrangement is a class of carbocationic rearrangements in which a hydrogen, aryl, or alkyl group migrates from one carbon to an adjacent electron-deficient (carbocationic) carbon atom to form a more stable carbocation.

#### Mechanism
The mechanism proceeds via the following steps:
1. **Generation of Initial Carbocation:** Protonation of an alcohol followed by the loss of a water molecule (or ionization of an alkyl halide/tosylate) generates a carbocation.
2. **1,2-Shift (Rearrangement):** A neighboring group ($\text{-H}$, $\text{-CH}_3$, or aryl group) shifts along with its bonding electron pair to the adjacent positively charged carbon atom (1,2-migration). This relieves ring strain or generates a more stable carbocation (e.g., secondary to tertiary).
3. **Deprotonation/Elimination:** Loss of a proton yields the final rearranged alkene or substitution product.

*Example (Pinacol-like or general alkyl shift):*
$$\text{R}_2\text{C(OH)-CHR'}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{R}_2\text{C}^+-\text{CH(OH)R'}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{1,2-shift}} \text{Rearranged Product}$$

```mermaid
graph LR
A[Alcohol Protonation] --> B[Formation of Initial Carbocation] --> C[1,2-Alkyl/Hydride Shift] --> D[More Stable Carbocation] --> E[Loss of Proton / Product]
```
proTip: Always check carbocation stability (3° > 2° > 1°) to predict the direction of the 1,2-shift in Wagner-Meerwein rearrangements.
